extraction.name: Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval)
extraction.description: A reproducible benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models. It contains 541 prompts, each with one or more verifiable instructions, covering 25 instruction types that can be checked using simple, interpretable, deterministic programs.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.citeAs: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, and Le Hou. Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911v1, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors identified 25 types of verifiable instructions and synthesized 541 prompts through four steps: generate base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended; use few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts; use another few-shot prompting approach to rephrase prompts for greater phrasing diversity; and manually check and edit every rephrased prompt. For baseline evaluation, GPT-4 and PaLM 2 Small responses were collected through API calls.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark consists of synthesized base prompts combined with randomly selected verifiable instructions, followed by few-shot filtering, rephrasing, and manual curation. The evaluation responses were obtained from GPT-4 and PaLM 2 Small through API calls.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: GPT-4 evaluation responses were collected in November 2023, and PaLM 2 Small evaluation responses were collected in August 2023. The collection timeframe for the benchmark prompts is not stated.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts were rephrased through few-shot prompting to increase phrasing diversity, then manually checked and edited individually. For loose instruction-following evaluation, each model response was evaluated under eight transformations: the original response; removal of common markdown font modifiers, especially * and **; removal of the first line; removal of the last line; and all combinations of those three removal operations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Few-shot prompting was used to identify and remove illogical prompts, addressing potential conflicts between appended instructions. Each rephrased prompt was subsequently checked and edited manually.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Instruction compliance in model responses is assessed automatically using simple heuristics and deterministic programs. For each response and verifiable instruction, the verification function returns True if the instruction is followed and False otherwise. The strict metric uses this result directly. The loose metric marks an instruction as followed if verification succeeds for any of eight transformed versions of the response. Human involvement is described as manually checking and editing synthesized prompts, rather than labeling model responses.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Strict verification can produce false negatives when responses contain acceptable variations, such as markdown bold formatting within a required ending phrase. Loose verification considers response transformations to reduce these false negatives, but can introduce false positives; for example, removing a response's first line can make a noncompliant word count appear compliant. The authors therefore treat the loose criterion as a complement to the strict criterion and report both prompt-level and instruction-level accuracy under each criterion.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Simple heuristics and interpretable, deterministic instruction-verification programs released with the IFEval code. No specific annotation software or library is named.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors release the evaluation code and prompts and plan future improvements to make prompts and verifiable instructions more related to real-world applications, expand the set of verifiable instructions, and support multimodal use cases. No versioning schedule, maintenance timeframe, named maintainers, or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper connects reliable instruction following to the safety and reliability of LLM applications. It notes that discrepancies or misunderstandings can produce unintended outputs with potentially serious consequences in settings such as healthcare or autonomous systems. The benchmark aims to make instruction-following evaluation clearer, more objective, reproducible, and fully automatic.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors describe IFEval as an unbiased evaluation approach based on objectively verifiable instructions. No empirical analysis of demographic or other dataset biases is reported.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are completely verifiable objectively and automatically, and edge cases remain difficult to judge. Strict verification can yield false negatives, while loose verification can introduce false positives. The authors identify the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions, relevance to real-world applications, and lack of multimodal support as areas for improvement. They also caution that the GPT-4 and PaLM 2 Small baseline results are not directly comparable because of a large difference in parameter counts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking the instruction-following ability of large language models. Researchers can compare models across instruction types and identify instructions that models commonly fail to follow. Evaluation reports prompt-level and instruction-level accuracy using both strict and loose verification; the loose criterion is intended to complement the strict criterion. GPT-4 and PaLM 2 Small results are provided as baselines.
